content.title: About
content.content: Lime soufflé is a light, airy dessert made from eggs, sugar, butter, and fresh lime juice. It has a bright citrus aroma and a delicate creamy texture that melts in the mouth.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Soufflé originates from French cuisine, where the word “soufflé” means “blown up”.
Lime contains more vitamin C than most other citrus fruits.
Traditionally, soufflé is served immediately after baking while the center is still slightly wobbly.
Achieving the perfect rise requires gently folding in beaten egg whites without deflating them.
Lime soufflé is often garnished with lime zest or mint for extra fragrance.

items.title: Rich in vitamin C
items.content: Lime provides a high amount of vitamin C, which supports the immune system and collagen synthesis.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: Compared with many desserts, soufflé contains little fat, especially when made with light butter.

items.title: Source of antioxidants
items.content: Lime flavonoids help combat free radicals and reduce oxidative stress.

items.title: Aids digestion
items.content: The acidity of lime stimulates gastric juice production, aiding digestion.

items.title: Provides lean protein
items.content: Egg whites in the soufflé supply high‑quality protein needed for tissue repair.

items.title: Egg allergy
items.content: Soufflé contains egg whites, which can trigger allergic reactions in sensitive individuals.

items.title: Lime acidity
items.content: High acidity may irritate the stomach of people with gastritis or ulcer disease.

items.title: Sugar content
items.content: Added sugar increases the dessert’s calories; those monitoring blood glucose should limit portions.

items.title: Requires immediate serving
items.content: Soufflé loses its rise quickly after baking, so it should be served right away or it becomes dense.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve lime soufflé warm, straight from the oven, often dusted with powdered sugar and garnished with fresh raspberries or mint. It pairs well with a light fruit sauce or a scoop of vanilla ice cream.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Soufflé is best enjoyed immediately. If needed, store in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 24 hours; reheat in the oven for 5‑7 minutes before serving to restore its airy texture.
